body:
Triage → `domain:services` · p1 · bug. Cross-domain possible; owning lane is `domain:services`.

**Anchoring, with the precedent that settles it.** The granularity path is owned end to end by `packages/services/service-analytics` — it resolves the granularity (`analytics-service.ts:1262`, `dataset-executor.ts:282-324`), picks native-SQL vs ObjectQL strategy, and reads the driver's `supports.queryDateGranularity` record. The actual date-bucket SQL is emitted in `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` (the `strftime` forms at `:4632`, quarter at `:4637`) ⇒ `domain:engine` if the fault turns out to be there. Two prior analytics cards of this exact shape — #5688 (native `dateGranularity` lowering) and #5520 (analytics 500 instead of 400 on a bad dimension) — are both labelled `domain:services`, so the lane follows precedent as well as the entry point.

**Dedup discharged.** The card notes the GitHub search API was rate-limited at filing time so its own scan could not complete. I ran it: **no open duplicate.** Nearest neighbours are all closed — #4033 (bucket label dropped from rows), #3650 (`ObjectQLStrategy` silently ignoring `timeDimensions[].dateRange`), #5688, #5520, #3588. The last two are the same *family* (analytics + granularity + a 500) and are worth reading before starting, but neither covers this.

## ⛔ Mandatory first step — it decides both the grade and the fix site

**Reproduce on Postgres before choosing where to fix.** The card measured this against the showcase dev app on better-sqlite3 and says so honestly ("worth checking whether the Postgres driver path differs"). That one reading forks the card:

- **Fails on both** ⇒ the fault is in the strategy/negotiation layer (`service-analytics`), the grade stands at p1, and the fix is single-lane.
- **SQLite only** ⇒ the fault is in `driver-sql`'s SQLite date-bucket emission, the card re-anchors to `domain:engine` as a cross-domain half, and the production grade drops to p2 (dev-app driver only).

⚠️ There is a live suspect for the SQLite-only branch already in the source: `sql-driver.ts:4580` — *"SQLite's strftime gained ISO week (%V) in 3.46 (2024-05-23); play it safe"* — i.e. this emitter already has known version-dependent behaviour. Read that block before reaching for the strategy layer.

**A second thing the reproduction must answer.** `sql-driver.ts:1448-1477` documents a real negotiation: a driver publishes `supports.queryDateGranularity`, and the engine reads that record and **falls back to in-engine bucketing** for a granularity the driver declines. A 500 `DATABASE_ERROR` means SQL was emitted and the database rejected it — so either the driver *claimed* `month` and emitted SQL the DB won't take, or something bypassed the capability check entirely. Which of those it is, is the root cause; ⛔ do not patch the SQL string without answering it, or the same class returns at `week` and `quarter`.

**Grade p1.** "Count by month" is not an exotic query — it is the default shape of most dashboard time charts, and it fails with a hard 500, not a degraded result. The card also records the downstream cost: two checklist items (`dashboards.drill-through-range`, `dashboards.empty-null-bucket-boundaries`) cannot be exercised at all because the underlying query 500s, so this one defect is blinding QA on a whole area. Held at p1 rather than p0 because a shipped Postgres deployment may be unaffected — which is exactly what the first step above settles.

**Note on why the unit pins did not catch it** — the card is right and this belongs in the fix's test plan: #3773 (date-bucket-parity) and #3839 (empty-group-parity) are green because they exercise bucketing at a layer that never reaches the real SQL driver. Whatever fix lands needs a test that goes through the actual driver, or the next regression is invisible the same way.

**QA-source**: #13404.

⭐ 这张卡是**带对照的现场报告**,不是猜测:同一 cube、同一会话下 `dimensions:[status]` 的分桶 **200 且与 `/data` 对得上**,畸形请求**在入口被 400 正确拒绝** ⇒ 入口校验器没问题,**故障在下游的 SQL 生成/执行**。⛔ 不要重新论证这一层。

⇒ **一个只加同层单测的修复,会连这个缺陷都复现不出来。** 本仓有 live-dialect 测试装置(`driver-sql` 的 `declareDialectCell`,跑真 PG / MySQL),这是本卡该用的形状。

os-dev-report

**#13714 — implemented. Draft PR: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/14112**

@baozhoutao — you run the deployment this was measured on, so the short version first: **your report is correct, your controls were the decisive evidence, and your hypothesis was wrong in a useful way.**

**It is not a date-truncation bug.** The `strftime` / `date_trunc` bucket expression is correct on every dialect. What the database refuses is the **alias**. Every analytics measure is addressed as `CUBE.MEASURE`, and that dotted name is handed to the SQL driver as the aggregation alias — the key you read the number back under. The driver bound it through a knex placeholder that *parses* an identifier rather than quoting one: it splits on the dot into `table.column`. So your query compiled to `count(*) as \`showcase_delivery\`.\`count\`` and was rejected before it ran.

**Your controls are what proved it.** The granularity is only the ROUTER: `NativeSQLStrategy` declines exactly when a `granularity` is present, and that face already wrote the alias correctly. So an un-bucketed query never reached the broken door and a bucketed one always did — which is precisely why `dimensions:[status]` was 200 and `granularity:'month'` was 500, on the same cube in the same session. Crossing the two axes on the pre-fix tree:

| alias | granularity | result |
|---|---|---|
| `n` | day / month / quarter / year | 200 |
| `showcase_delivery.count` | none at all | **500** |
| `showcase_delivery.count` | month | **500** |

The middle row is the one that settles it — no bucket anywhere, same 500.

**What to expect in your deployment.** All of `day`/`month`/`quarter`/`year` are fixed together, not just `month`. `week` on SQLite was never broken this way: the driver declines it up front and the engine buckets it in memory, which is why it kept working. The two blocked checklist items (`dashboards.drill-through-range`, `dashboards.empty-null-bucket-boundaries`) should be exercisable again once this lands.

**What I could not verify, and who can.** Everything below was measured on **better-sqlite3 — your driver**. Postgres and MySQL are pinned by the same suite but were **NOT executed here** (no live servers in this container); CI's live-dialect matrix job runs them. The defect lives in knex's shared formatter rather than in any dialect, so both are broken by construction and repaired by construction — but that is an argument, not a reading, and I am not presenting the SQLite green as a measurement for them.

If you can re-run the original request against your deployment once this lands, that is the one confirmation nobody else can give.

---

### For the PM

**Dedup (step 0, the filer could not finish it).** Repo-scoped REST list endpoint, **436 open issues scanned** (PRs excluded), grepped locally for `timeDimension` / `granularity` / `date bucket` / `date_trunc` / `strftime` / analytics-month-week. **Zero duplicates** — the only hit was #13714 itself. `/search/issues` was never used.

**Root cause.** Not the granularity clause. `SqlDriver.aggregate` bound the caller's aggregation `alias` through knex's `??`, which parses an identifier rather than quoting one and splits on `.`. Every analytics measure is `CUBE.MEASURE`, so every cube query reaching that door carried a dotted alias. The granularity only ROUTES the query there — `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` declines exactly on a granularity, and that face already emitted the alias correctly.

**Answering the anchoring comment's two questions directly.** The lane is `domain:engine`, not `domain:services`: the fault is entirely in `packages/drivers/driver-sql`. And it is neither of the two branches that comment forecast — not "fails on both" *(a strategy/negotiation fault)* and not "SQLite only" *(a SQLite date-bucket emission fault)*. It is **dialect-independent** and lives in the alias position, not the bucket. The capability negotiation is working correctly throughout: the driver claimed `month`, emitted a correct `strftime`, and the statement died on the alias.

**Ablation, direction predicted before running.** Mutation = the file restored to its `62a137bae` blob; confirmed on disk by blob hash and by both marker counts moving, and in `dist/` by `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs --absent` for the cross-package leg. Restore proven by state (whole-tree `git status --porcelain` clean, blob back to HEAD, markers back, preflight positive).

| suite | mutated | restored |
|---|---|---|
| driver-sql alias identity | **10 red**, 3 green | 13 green, 2 unprovisioned |
| service-analytics granularity route | **12 red**, 1 green | 13 green |

Green in **both** directions, so ⛔ declared controls and not ablation evidence: `week` on SQLite (both suites), and driver-sql's two bare-alias controls. The prediction held unrevised.

The ablation also caught an overclaim of mine: the second suite's un-bucketed cases reddened too, because that harness sets `nativeSql: false` and forces them down the same door. I renamed them for what they measure rather than leaving them labelled as a reproduction of the reporter's controls.

**A pin swap worth flagging.** I first wrote the end-to-end pin as a dogfood `bootStack` HTTP suite. Its build closure could not be brought up in this container — parallel agents' full-workspace builds repeatedly cleaned the `dist/` directories it needs, across four attempts. Rather than ship a test I had never executed, I replaced it with a service-analytics pin that runs here **against better-sqlite3, the reported driver**, and cites the already-green `native-sql-granularity-decline.test.ts` for the routing half instead of duplicating it.

**Gates.** Re-derived from the actual diff (both sections read whole; re-derived after the diff changed and again after `git fetch origin main` — stable at 36). **35 green / 36**, on `7d20ebda1`. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` first exited 3 naming a missing full-workspace `dist/`; I built that closure (70/70) and both re-ran green. `check-test-completeness` stays **NOT MEASURED** — it grades a saved `turbo run test` log, a CI artifact.

## 已落地(PR #14112,`9e1b2de73`)—— 但**本卡的假设被证伪**,这一点比修复本身更值得记

⭐ **不是日期截断问题。** 卡的 Notes 写的是 *"Likely a date-truncation SQL emission issue for the granularity clause"* —— 实测为假。

真因:`SqlDriver.aggregate` 把调用方的聚合**别名**经 knex 的 `??` 占位符绑定,而 `??` **不是引号包装,是标识符解析** —— 它按 `.` 把值切成 `table.column` 再逐段加引号。而每个 analytics 度量在线上的名字就是 `<cube>.<measure>`,`ObjectQLStrategy` 把这个带点的名字**原样**当作驱动层别名(因为那是调用方读回自己数字的键)。于是语句编译成:

```
count(*) as `showcase_delivery`.`count`     ← 任何方言下都不是合法 SQL
```

**在跑之前就被拒**,`aggregate` 的终端信封把它包成 `DATABASE_ERROR`/500。

## ⭐ granularity 是**路由器**,不是故障点 —— 这一条解释了卡里的**控制项**

`NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` **恰好在有 granularity 时拒收**,而那张脸自己手写 `AS "<measure>"`(一个带引号的标识符,本来就是对的)。⇒ **未分桶的 cube 查询根本到不了这道坏门**,分桶的每次都到。

⇒ 卡里那三条「同一 session 里成功的控制项」不是巧合,是**同一个机制的另一半**。⭐ 一个能同时解释**红**与**绿**的诊断才是根因;只解释红的是猜测。

⚠️ **推论**:一个瞄准 `buildDateBucketExpr` 的修复 —— 也就是卡建议的方向 —— **什么都不会改**。

## 卡的另外两句,一句答了一句仍然成立

- *"worth checking whether the Postgres driver path differs"* ⇒ **不差**。`wrapString` 的切分住在 knex 的**共享 formatter**,不在任何方言里,所以缺陷按构造是方言无关的。修复对全矩阵下钉:SQLite 内嵌实测,Postgres/MySQL 经 CI 的 `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` 道确认(该道在本 PR 上绿)。
- *"the date-bucket parity pins are green … they exercise the bucketing at a layer that does not hit the real SQL driver"* ⇒ **成立,而且原因比卡说的更精确**:那些 pin 的参照侧把行按别名当作**普通 JS 对象键**来排,而点号在对象键里是惰性的;并且它们的探针别名都是**裸名**。⇒ 唯一能打破 SQL 面的那个输入,恰是它们从不提供的那个。⛔ 它们是本卡的**声明控制项**(必须保持绿),不是关于本卡的证据。

## 围栏做对了一处,值得记

修复只把**别名位**改成 `client.wrapIdentifier`(knex 自己逐段调用的同一个函数,所以方言引号与宿主 `wrapIdentifier` 钩子照旧生效);**列引用**继续走 `??`,仍可带限定。⛔ 把「整串加引号」推广到引用位会打断该驱动发出的每一个合法 `table.column`。

## 衍生卡

**#14113**(Turso 的 `RemoteTransport` 用 `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` 拒绝点号,同类不同面)已按车道表路由到 **`domain:engine`**(`packages/drivers/*` 归 engine),p2,`pm:queue`。⚠️ 本 PR **不会**顺带修好它 —— 两处是独立的门。
